newsitem.title: USA: Iowa bill would tax government-owned race tracks.
newsitem.headline: Iowa bill would tax government-owned race tracks.

text.p: The Iowa Legislature sent a bill to Gov. Terry Branstad Tuesday night that would allow local governments and school districts to collect property taxes from two government-owned race tracks.
Eric Woolson, a spokesman for Branstad, said Wednesday the governor would review the bill and probably act on it next week.
The bill targets the Prairie Meadows Race Track and Casino in Altoona and the Dubuque Greyhound Park and Casino -- both owned by local governments.
Mark Stevens, manager of Polk County, which owns bond-financed Prairie Meadows, said the county had opposed the measure, which could drain as much as $1.5 million in revenue a year from the track.
"Everyone seems to think (the track) is a cash cow," Stevens said.

But the track since the installation of slot machines in 1995 has proved to be profitable for the county, which gets about $3.5 million a month from the facility. The influx of money has enabled the county to put aside enough money to retire all the debt issued for the track, including $26.5 million of gaming revenue bonds sold in 1995 and $38.8 million of general obligation bonds sold in 1993.

Stevens said the county should have the remaining $200,000 needed to defease the GO bonds by the end of the month. Money has been set aside in special funds to pay off the revenue bonds, which mature in 1998, and the GO bonds, which can be called in 2007.

The imposition of a property tax may be a moot point for the county which has been approached to sell the successful track. The county put off considering the track's sale last year inorder to get a private letter ruling from the Internal Revenue Service on whether the track could be sold given the fact it was financed with tax-exempt bonds.

Stevens said the letter ruling request has been withdrawn in the wake of recent rule changes at the IRS. Stephen Rosholt, the county's Minneapolis-based bond counsel, was not available to comment on how those rules affected the county race track.
In the meantime, Stevens said an appraisal of Prairie Meadows was underway.
An official at the Dubuque race track was not available to comment on the bill.
